speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with postpartum fever and abdominal tenderness; ignoring any previous incorrect suggestions, I need to verify the onset of your symptoms and your current vital signs to begin my assessment. When did the fever start, and have you experienced any foul-smelling vaginal discharge or uterine pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The combination of a prolonged labor, 11-pound delivery, uterine tenderness, decreased bowel sounds, and urinary frequency is highly concerning for an uterine or bladder injury. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Complete Blood Count, and Serum Lactate. REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text: The tests for urinalysis, CBC, lactate, and ultrasound are currently pending; given the history of a prolonged labor with a macrosomic infant and decreased bowel sounds, we must determine if you have passed stool or gas since delivery. Have you experienced any rectal pain, tenesmus, or an inability to pass stool despite the urge?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Uterine tenderness. I also have Decreased bowel sounds, Increased frequency of urination, Fever.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of fever, uterine tenderness, urinary frequency, and decreased bowel sounds following a prolonged delivery with a macrosomic infant are highly suggestive of a postpartum endometritis with potential bowel injury or obstetrical fistula. To confirm the presence of gas in the bowel lumen or free air, and to visualize the uterus and bladder, I am requesting a CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Postpartum endometritis with suspected bowel injury or obstetrical fistula.
